data.outcome_summary: This OECD PISA 2022 Canada factsheet summarizes how 15-year-old students in Canada performed in mathematics, reading, and science, and how results changed relative to earlier cycles (notably 2018 and 2012). It reports mean performance trends, proficiency-level distributions (e.g., shares at Level 2+ and Level 5/6), and within-Canada gaps by socio-economic status, gender, and immigrant background, alongside contextual indicators such as belonging, discipline, safety, parental involvement, and COVID-related learning disruptions. The assessment uses two hour-long tests with different subject combinations across students, plus student and school questionnaires; achievement estimates are drawn from the OECD PISA 2022 Database tables. The factsheet also notes that response rates declined and fell below technical targets in several provinces, with analyses indicating limited bias from school non-participation but a small upward bias from student non-response. No student-level ML models are trained or evaluated in this document; it is a descriptive reporting of PISA results and policy-relevant patterns.
